notes: Closest to the reference: tracks a max exemplar timestamp and hasExemplar flag on memSeries, updated on commit, WAL replay and snapshot load, and uses it in both gc paths with minValidTime; unlike the reference it does not protect exemplars before commit, and its tests are broad (v1/v2, selected/stale/ordinary compaction with a real checkpoint) but skip snapshots and use a slightly hacky &Head{} unit test.

Closely mirrors the reference by tracking the max exemplar timestamp and a has-exemplar flag on memSeries, so zero and negative timestamps work. It also sets them on WAL and snapshot replay, so protection survives restarts. It releases chunks correctly in gcSeries, and its tests cover V1/V2, selected/stale/ordinary compaction and restart. One gap: the timestamp is recorded at commit rather than append, leaving a small pre-commit window the reference closes.

Storage-lookup approach with gcWithKeep and gcSeriesWithKeep wrappers that keep existing signatures, plus a removeAllChunks helper; tests are strong (selected and stale, CompactHead plus restart with snapshot, replayed samples released again, zero and negative gc cases) but do not exercise AppenderV2, and the lock-coupling concern remains.

Uses the same exemplar-storage lookup as C2, adding gcWithKeep and gcSeriesWithKeep wrappers that make the call graph noisier, with the same lock-nesting and ring-eviction caveats. Chunk release and metrics are handled correctly. Tests are thorough: snapshot on/off, a second compaction plus restart, replayed samples being released again, and zero/negative cutoffs.

Retains series in both gc and gcSeries by looking up the newest exemplar in the circular exemplar storage against minValidTime; this works, including for replayed and snapshot-restored exemplars, but it ties GC to the concrete storage type and takes the global exemplar lock while holding the stripe and series locks; tests cover v1/v2, zero and negative timestamps, chunk metrics and restart with and without snapshot, but not stale or ordinary compaction.

Takes the exemplar-storage lookup approach with a retain(labels) callback and a changed gcSeries signature. It works, with the same lock-nesting and buffer-eviction caveats as C2 and C3. Tests are strong: V1/V2 appenders, zero/negative timestamps, the cutoff moving past the exemplar, and restart with and without the memory snapshot.

Uses the same storage-lookup approach through a keepSeries hook on stripeSeries, with a clean dropInOrderChunks helper that releases chunks and counts them correctly; it shares the same lock coupling and gives no pre-commit protection, and its tests cover gc timestamps, selected and stale compaction and restart, but not AppenderV2 or snapshots.

Decides retention by looking up the newest exemplar in the circular exemplar storage, which naturally survives restarts. The cost is a series-lock to exemplar-storage-lock nesting and dependence on the concrete storage type. Series also lose protection once their exemplar is evicted from the ring buffer. Tests are solid but skip AppenderV2 and the memory snapshot, and the stale case has no restart.
